chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: Editing this base alone will not produce a reproducible TF-dependent change in TERT output in relevant cells.
The variant may be a passenger, may act through a mechanism not mediated by allele-specific TF binding, or may have no measurable effect.
falsified_if: Isogenic editing produces a reproducible allele-dependent TERT effect that is accompanied by differential occupancy of a specific TF and is reduced by perturbing that TF.

chains.title: Alt-allele gain of GABPA binding alters TERT promoter output

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to the alt allele using an ETV5-mapped ETS model, not a GABPA-specific model. GABPA has variant-overlapping ChIP peaks only in other biosamples; the shared ETS prediction also applies to ETV2, ETV3, and FLI1, so the evidence does not identify GABPA as the changing factor.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE with activity-associated signals in ENCODE biosamples, but the reported maxima do not establish activity in glioblastoma cells.
The variant is in the TERT promoter region at the TERT transcription start site.
GABPA is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context, but occupancy at this site in that context has not been demonstrated.

This model proposes that the alt-allele binding gain changes TERT promoter output; increased TERT transcription could contribute to tumor-associated telomerase activity. General literature supports increased transcription from TERT promoter mutations, but does not establish this variant's effect, its TF mechanism, or a disease effect, particularly in bladder cancer.

predictions: In relevant glioblastoma cells, the alt allele should show greater GABPA occupancy than the ref allele.

If GABPA is the causal factor and acts to increase promoter output here, editing to the alt allele should increase TERT transcription, and GABPA perturbation should diminish that allele-dependent effect.
falsified_if: A relevant-cell assay finds no alt-biased GABPA occupancy, while detecting the candidate factor's occupancy adequately.
Isogenic editing shows no reproducible TERT output difference, or any difference is unaffected by GABPA perturbation.

chains.title: Loss of ref-favored TGIF2 binding changes TERT promoter output

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to the ref allele using a PKNOX2-mapped homeodomain model, not a TGIF2-specific model. TGIF2 has a variant-overlapping ChIP peak only in another biosample, so occupancy and the predicted allele effect are unconfirmed in glioblastoma.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE with activity-associated signals in ENCODE biosamples, but glioblastoma-specific activity is not established.
The variant is in the TERT promoter region at the TERT transcription start site.
TGIF2 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context, but the available variant-overlapping ChIP evidence is from HepG2, not glioblastoma.

This model proposes that reduced TGIF2 binding on the alt allele changes TERT promoter output. A repressive role for TGIF2 at this site is an untested assumption; general TERT promoter literature does not establish a TGIF2-mediated or disease effect for this variant.

predictions: If TGIF2 occupies this site in relevant glioblastoma cells, occupancy should be greater on the ref allele.
If TGIF2 represses TERT here, the alt allele should increase TERT output and TGIF2 perturbation should reduce the allele-dependent difference.
falsified_if: A relevant-cell assay finds no ref-biased TGIF2 occupancy, while detecting TGIF2 occupancy adequately.
TGIF2 perturbation does not affect an allele-dependent TERT output difference, or the direction of the output change contradicts the proposed repressive model.

chains.title: Loss of ref-favored ZNF143 binding changes TERT promoter output

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX, using a ZNF143-specific model, predicts stronger binding to the ref allele. ZNF143 has a variant-overlapping ChIP peak in GM12878, but occupancy in glioblastoma is not shown.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE with activity-associated signals in ENCODE biosamples, but glioblastoma-specific activity is not established.
The variant is in the TERT promoter region at the TERT transcription start site.
ZNF143 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context, but the variant-overlapping ChIP evidence is from GM12878 rather than glioblastoma.

This model proposes that reduced ZNF143 binding on the alt allele changes TERT promoter output. Whether ZNF143 activates or represses TERT at this site is not established, and the general TERT promoter literature does not demonstrate a ZNF143-mediated or disease effect for this variant.

predictions: In relevant glioblastoma cells, ZNF143 occupancy should be greater on the ref allele.
The allele-dependent TERT output change should depend on ZNF143; its direction cannot be predicted from the supplied evidence because ZNF143's regulatory role at this site is unknown.
falsified_if: A relevant-cell assay finds no ref-biased ZNF143 occupancy, while detecting ZNF143 occupancy adequately.
ZNF143 perturbation leaves any allele-dependent TERT output effect unchanged.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent TERT change that depends on one of the candidate TFs.

next_experiment: The cheapest direct discriminator for the top two hypotheses (H0 and H1) is allele-resolved GABPA CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag in a relevant glioblastoma model. H1 predicts greater GABPA occupancy on the alt allele; H0 predicts no reproducible TF-mediated allelic occupancy effect. A positive occupancy result would still need functional follow-up to establish an effect on TERT output.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.

Conclusions: Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
The genetic landscape of familial melanoma is heterogeneous.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
BackgroundMutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

ConclusionThe rs2853669 C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
The prognostic relevance of CDKN2A deletion may vary according to TERTp status, particularly for OS.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr5:1295135:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 18 occupied (14 with a strong site), 5 of 145 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 554 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 1 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th.
